lesson_title: The Science of Not Enough: What Economics Studies
hook_text: You've been doing economics since your first week of pocket money.
clip_script: The entire subject fits in one line: everyone wants more than there is — so now what? Test it at the tuckshop with sixty rand. The wants queue up instantly: the pie, the cold drink, airtime, saving toward the sneakers. Sixty rand cannot cover the queue — and the moment one want is fed, another shuffles forward to take its place. That self-refilling queue is what economists mean by unlimited wants. Now watch your aunt's weekend car wash: the yard she uses, the cousins she pays, the pressure hose she bought, and her own nerve in setting it all up — those are the four factors of production, working in an ordinary driveway. The yard collects rent, the cousins collect wages, the hose money earns interest, and the risk-taker keeps the profit. Make, swap, use — production, exchange, consumption. The grand vocabulary of economics describes a driveway perfectly. That's the subject: the science of not-enough, run on people.
visual_style: Fast-cut morning-street energy: a tuckshop counter with wants popping up as floating labels that multiply when one is ticked off, then a driveway car wash where four glowing tags — RENT, WAGES, INTEREST, PROFIT — attach to the yard, the washers, the hose and the owner.
pacing: Quick label-pop rhythm through the tuckshop, slowing to four deliberate tag-lands at the car wash, snap ending on the one-line definition.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and put names to what you already do.
